prohibitedInitialActions: Do not assume isolated user request overrides project architecture
Do not install packages without checking existing dependencies
Do not modify production code or database schema

require: avoid inventing new patterns when approved pattern exists

beforeAddingDependency: Check whether existing dependency already solves the problem
Check whether native platform/framework already supports the requirement
Check whether dependency conflicts with architecture

require: avoid decorative UI that reduces clarity
avoid: visually impressive interface at the cost of usability

steps: Commit the generated drizzle/ migration with the schema change
drizzleNotes: The schema is hand-written TypeScript in src/db/schema/index.ts using pgTable. There is no schema DSL file and no generated client.
`pnpm db:generate` turns schema changes into drizzle/ migration SQL. It never touches the database; `pnpm db:check` validates migration files and also never connects.
Everything under drizzle/ is generated output — never hand-edit it.
There is NO schema-drift gate: nothing can verify a live database matches the schema. Shipping a generated migration alongside every schema edit is the compensating control, so do not skip it.
Only `pnpm db:migrate` may be applied to a real database. `pnpm db:push` bypasses migration history and is for local throwaway experiments only.
forbid: create destructive migrations without explicit approval

securityWorkflow: Before implementing security-sensitive functionality, AI must inspect: authentication, authorization, RBAC, session handling, input validation, server-side authorization, database access, file uploads, sensitive data, audit logging, rate limiting. Never rely on UI-level restrictions as the security boundary.
testingWorkflow: AI-generated changes must be validated according to project's testing standards. Determine whether change requires: unit tests, integration tests, database tests, server-action tests, component tests, E2E tests. For critical workflows (login, student creation, student editing, attendance, fee/payment operations, role permissions, reports), prefer end-to-end coverage where appropriate.
